title: One-Click SDK Runner: proposal & sample flows (draft)
content:
Goal:
Deliver a frictionless first-run for engineers who want to try Redwood SDKs in <5 minutes. The concept is a One-Click SDK Runner (local or cloud-backed) that scaffolds a small app, runs a canonical request, and wires basic telemetry so the user sees success and cost/latency signals immediately.

Why this is different from existing quickstarts:
- Current quickstarts are docs-first and require copy/paste plus environment setup.
- This runner is an opinionated, executable quickstart: click -> scaffold -> run -> inspect. Low switching cost.
- Focus on experiential telemetry (latency, token usage, model chosen) so users understand the economics right away.

Primary users and scenarios:
- New SDK evaluators (individual devs, startups) who want immediate gratification.
- Platform/infra engineers validating private deployments: scaffold can target hosted or local/private endpoints.
- Workshop/demo leads who need reproducible ephemeral apps.

MVP feature list (tentative):
1) CLI: redwood-run init --runtime=python|node --target=hosted|private --example=chat|embeddings
   - Scaffolds a tiny app with README and sample inputs.
   - Adds .env.example with REDWOOD_API_KEY or PRIVATE_ENDPOINT config.
2) One-click Web Runner (optional for MVP): a tiny hosted sandbox that executes the scaffold remotely using ephemeral creds (limit usage).
3) Baseline example flows: chat-turn, single-text-embedding, rerank sample. Each runs a canonical input and prints structured output.
4) Telemetry: local console summary + optional opt-in telemetry upload to show latency, total tokens, model name, billing estimate. Event names: sdk.run.start, sdk.run.success, sdk.run.error, sdk.run.telemetryOptIn
5) Safety/error helpers: common errors mapped to suggestions (bad key, network, model mismatch).
6) 'Explain' mode: short explanation after run describing what happened (model used, why latency might be high, caching suggestions).

Sample CLI session (draft):
$ redwood-run init --runtime=python --target=hosted --example=chat
Scaffold created at ./redwood-sample-chat
Run the example: cd redwood-sample-chat && redwood-run run --open
Running example with model: gpt-small-open (quantized)
Tokens: prompt=48, completion=92, est_cost=$0.0007
Latency (p95): 180ms
Output: { "response": "Hi! How can I help today?" }

Design notes / UX decisions:
- Keep the scaffold minimal: single file + README, not a framework-specific opinion. Use tiny serverless patterns (Flask/Express) so users can iterate.
- Provide both interactive mode (opens REPL-like console) and headless run for CI/workshops.
- The CLI should auto-detect REDWOOD_API_KEY, but prompt securely if missing. For private endpoints, allow --endpoint flag and store in local config at ./redwood/config.json (encrypted by OS keystore? TBD).
- Make telemetry opt-in by default with clear description what is collected. Allow --telemetry=on/off.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- First-time user can run an example and see a successful generation and a short summary in <= 5 minutes (measured in user test).
- CLI scaffolds code that runs without modification on macOS and Linux with a single package install step.
- Telemetry opt-in flow works and events are visible in Console (basic dashboard).
- Error mapping captures the top 6 failure modes and provides actionable suggestions.

Instrumentation & metrics to track post-launch:
- Completion rate: percent of users who run the scaffold after init.
- Time-to-first-success: minutes from install to first successful generation.
- Telemetry opt-in rate.
- Error rates and top error messages.
- Conversion: percent of users who call hosted API after using runner (correlate with API keys created).

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (internal): prototype CLI + 2 examples. Test with eng-developer-experience and solutions-eng. Deadline: 6 weeks.
- Phase 1 (beta): expose to certain signups and docs site + workshop. Collect UX feedback and metrics.
- Phase 2 (public): add Web Runner, expand examples (private deployment templates), pair with docs and short screencast.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Private endpoint credential handling: do we offer OS keystore integration (macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager) in MVP or defer? (risk: dev effort vs security comfort)
- Hosted Web Runner: do we provide ephemeral API keys or route via our sandbox account? Need rate limits and billing guardrails.
- Model selection: should runner pick a lowest-cost compatible model by default or a mid-tier recommended model? Need product to sign off.
- Acceptance by security/compliance for examples that talk to private endpoints — add warnings and docs.

Implementation sketch (files):
- cli/ (redwood-run)
  - commands: init, run, info, doctor
- templates/
  - python/chat.py, node/chat.js, readme.md, .env.example
- telemetry/
  - events map, local buffer, upload worker (opt-in)
- docs/
  - quickstart.md, troubleshooting.md, workshop-guide.md

Security & privacy notes:
- Telemetry must not contain user prompts or generated content. Only meta: model name (anonymized?), token counts, latency, error codes, region.
- Provide automated scrubber and allow offline-only mode (no telemetry).

Compatibility and migration:
- Should work with hosted Redwood API and accept PRIV_ENDPOINT env for Redwood Private installs.
- Provide simple migration doc for customers who want to adopt this in their internal developer portals (how to fork templates, customize telemetry endpoint).

Edge-case flows to handle (developer pain points):
- Local dev behind a proxy (HTTP_PROXY handling)
- Partial responses / streaming: runner will show streamed partials; ability to toggle streaming in config.
- Rate limit response: show fallback suggestion to reduce batch size/sequence length or switch model tier.

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Check with console team on telemetry ingestion schema (ping @Drew).
- Wireframe quick modal that summarizes cost in simple terms (tokens -> $ estimate) for the web runner.
- Create a short script that verifies sample runs in CI for each PR (CI test harness).
- Link to internal evals repo for example prompts that exercise failure modes (CONFLUENCE LINK).

Next steps (this week):
- Align with product on default model selection and telemetry policy (owner: Lina).
- Prototype CLI scaffolder using cookiecutter-style templates (owner: Ethan).
- Draft workshop guide for beta users and internal demos (owner: Priya).

References and related tickets:
- DEX-880: quickstart telemetry schema (defines sdk.run.* events)
- DEX-904: One-Click runner spec (this ticket, prototype)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/842 (initial CLI parser)
notes_summary: Draft design doc for a One-Click SDK Runner: CLI + optional web sandbox to scaffold and execute short SDK examples with opt-in telemetry. MVP acceptance criteria, rollout plan, open questions, and implementation sketch included. Owners: Priya, Ethan, Lina.
